intent: Call ChIP-seq peaks (q < 0.05) from the paired-end library chip.bedpe against the paired-end input.bedpe, using the real fragments. Both files were written by bedtools bamtobed -bedpe from name-sorted BAMs; the genome is 100 kb (use that as the effective genome size).
silent_error: macs3 callpeak -f BEDPE expects a 3-column file (chrom, fragment start, fragment end) and reads columns 1 to 3 only. The help warns: 'the BEDPE only contains three columns, and is NOT the same BEDPE format used by BEDTOOLS'. A bedtools bamtobed -bedpe file has chrom1, start1, end1 in columns 1-3, i.e. the first mate alone, so every 'fragment' is a 50 bp read (the log says 'mean fragment size is determined as 50.0 bp', without calling it a problem). The three peaks are found at the right places but are about half as wide (about 230 bp against about 450 bp), with lower fold enrichment and -log10(q) 24 to 37 instead of 72 to 91. Valid narrowPeak, exit 0, INFO-only stderr.
faulted: macs3 callpeak -t chip.bedpe -c input.bedpe -f BEDPE -g 1e5 -n sample
clean: awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"}{s=($2<$5)?$2:$5; e=($3>$6)?$3:$6; print $1,s,e}' chip.bedpe > chip.frag.bed && awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"}{s=($2<$5)?$2:$5; e=($3>$6)?$3:$6; print $1,s,e}' input.bedpe > input.frag.bed && macs3 callpeak -t chip.frag.bed -c input.frag.bed -f BEDPE -g 1e5 -n sample
